task_card.title: LTX spatial upscaler - bench evaluation as the SeedVR2 successor

next_action.description: Start MPI-580 (the plugin mechanism) - read its card description, which is thorough and current, then write its plan.md. It has no plan yet and it blocks MPI-579. Design the contribution point for BOTH dropdown kinds at once, because MPI-507 reuses it unchanged and generalising later is the build-it-twice failure the umbrella exists to prevent. Three extensions, not one: a plugin contributes an ENTRY to the EXISTING MpiToolOptionsUpscale dropdown; a selected entry contributes its own CONTROLS with a hidden 0-1 mapping; and a plugin can be required by a Flow and share deps with a ModelDef. Surface the product question to Fabio early - what the Library row says for a user without LTX - because it shapes the install UI and only he can answer it.

key_decisions: A MECHANISM MUST NOT RIDE ON A PRODUCT CARD, and this repo has the scar: MPI-506 owned 'SeedVR2 as three plugins AND the mechanism'; SeedVR2 was dropped, MPI-506 closed `complete`, the mechanism was never built, and MPI-507 went on sitting `blocked` on a closed card. Verified in code, not inferred - pluginsRegistry.js holds one plugin and MpiToolOptionsUpscale has no plugin awareness. Hence MPI-580.

IT IS NOT A NEW DROPDOWN. Fabio corrected the first write-up: the History workspace Upscale tool ALREADY has a model dropdown (MpiToolOptionsUpscale, shared by image and video via `kind`, listing None + loaded assets). The work is an ENTRY in it, and the controls that appear when it is selected.

BOTH SLIDERS SHOW 0-1 AND THE MAPPING IS HIDDEN - 'occulted from the user, as per usual'. denoise 0-1 -> sigmas 0.50-0.85, default UI 0.5 (0.675 is exactly mid-range); prompt strength 0-1 -> cfg 1-3, default UI 0. cfg defaults to the no-guidance end deliberately: 'Most upscaling jobs do not want too much change anyway.' A recommendation of 3 was overruled - do not restore it.

THERE IS NOTHING TO DOWNLOAD. ltx23-spatial-upscaler is already in assetDeps.js, already on R2, and already in the `dependencies` of BOTH LTX 2.3 tiers in models.js - so an LTX user is satisfied for free and pluginAvailability() gives that with no new code. Fabio predicted it. The corollary is the open product question: a non-LTX user faces a plugin whose install is the whole LTX stack.

MPI-557 ADOPTS THE UPSCALER - 'the plug-in will be a requirement for it, as it is a flow'. So the plugin has a second consumer before it ships, and Flow-requires-plugin became a phase-1 requirement rather than a later idea.
constraints: A PEER SESSION IS LIVE IN THIS TREE and owns MPI-504 plus js/data/modelConstants/models.js - never stage them. guard-claim blocks a write to a bare shared filename (a `cd` into a task folder made `validation.md` ambiguous and it blocked); write repo-root-relative paths, and claim under state/files/ when editing a card file whose basename a peer also holds.

EVENT RECORDS ARE {schema, id, type, at, actor, summary} - writing {at, actor, task, type, summary} passes json.load and fails the board validator on two counts per line. Run <mpi-lib>/scripts/validate_board.py after any board or event write.

THE GPU LEASE IS MACHINE-GLOBAL and the peer holds it for krea2 batches. Wrap sampler runs: python <mpi-lib>/scripts/gpu_lease.py run -- <cmd>, as a BACKGROUND Bash call - a foreground wait dies with the session and reads as success. Bench is :8188; no bench work should be needed now.
The Bash tool BLOCKS heredocs and backslash-newline continuations - write python with the Write tool and run it by path. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is EMPTY in Bash; use the absolute plugin path.
NEVER take Fabio's app instance - `npm run app:isolated` spins your own on a free port with its own profile. :3000 is his live session.
